newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HBG acquires Higgs & Hill unit.
newsitem.headline: HBG acquires Higgs & Hill unit.

text.p: Construction firm Hollandsche Beton Groep NV said on Tuesday it had reached agreement on the takeover of the construction division of UK builder Higgs & Hill for some 80 million guilders.

"The envisaged takeover will be finalised as soon as the shareholders of Higgs & Hill PLC -- listed on the London Stock Exchange -- have approved (the deal) at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting to be held in January 1997," HBG said in a statement.
"The takeover involves a sum of some 80 million guilders," it added.
It said the takeover deal would not include Higgs & Hill's housing and project development divisions, which woulld be continued by Higgs & Hill PLC under the name Swan Hill Group.

HBG said that Higgs & Hill's construction division was expected to post turnover of some 525 million guilders over the current financial year, but that the activities would probably close 1996 with a loss.
In 1995 the construction division booked a pre-tax loss of some 20 million guilders, including an extraordinary charge of 17 million guilders for restructuring and bad debt provisions, HBG said.
HBG is active in the United Kingdom through its subsidiaries Nuttall (marine engineering) Kyle Stewart and GA (general building), HAM (dredging) and Tebodin (engineering consultancy).
"With the Higgs & Hill Construction acquisition, HBG will strengthen the Group's position in the UK construction market," HBG said.
It said the acquisition would boost its UK turnover to 1.8 billion guilders from a current 1.2 billion guilders or 22 percent of group turnover.
"The acquisition is in line with HBG's strategic plan which aims at achieving a balanced spread of the construction activities both geographically and across the different sectors, HBG said.
